requirement:
Marks an agent request that can still accept reusable context before adding node contents.

```rust,ignore
pub struct ContextPhase;
```
rationale:
structural: The only structural obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.ContextPhase` is the prescribed declaration `pub struct ContextPhase;`, a public unit struct that marks the request phase. An alternative such as a private or non-unit type, or an enum with a different name, could behave the same at runtime. It would still violate the declared signature, so this obligation needs implementation evidence. The root `crates/trust-but-verify/src/procedure.rs#struct[ContextPhase]` is declared as `pub struct ContextPhase;` and carries the {impl} marker. I checked the declaration itself, not just the marker comment. The sentence about accepting reusable context before node contents describes how other request types use the marker. That is behavior of the types that use it, not a separate structural clause on this type. It needs no further root.

behavioral: `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.ContextPhase` contains no MUST, SHOULD or MAY clause. It declares `pub struct ContextPhase;`, a public marker type for an `Ask` request that can still accept context. Its only independently checkable obligation is that this public type exists with that shape and is exported.

`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` is marked `{test}` for the SDK export requirements. It generates rustdoc for the SDK, compares the exported paths and item kinds against the specified inventory, and asserts that nothing is missing or unexpected. Removing `ContextPhase`, making it private, or turning it into a different kind of item would fail that assertion. The same test also checks that the Habeas consumer compiles against the SDK.

What the phase does is that `context` is available only on `Ask<..., ContextPhase>`. That belongs to the refining requirements `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.phases` and `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.Ask`. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/procedure.rs` carries `{impl}` references for those requirements on the `Ask<..., ContextPhase>` impl block. Their obligations need no separate test here. The declaration in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/procedure.rs#struct[ContextPhase]` has no conditional or transformation of its own that could need a behavioral test. No gap is found.
